newsitem.title: USA: IMF rejects talk of early Kenya loan discussions.
newsitem.headline: IMF rejects talk of early Kenya loan discussions.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund, still worried about corruption in Kenya, on Thursday shot down talk of discussions on a new loan deal.

An IMF spokesman said the fund was happy to offer Kenya technical advice, but Nairobi had to deal with "governance issues" before talks could start on reopening the Enhanced Structural Adjustment Facility (ESAF) suspended last week.
"The fund is ready to assist Kenya with policy advice, including developing a framework to deal with the current situation," the spokesman said.

But he added: "Any formal fund involvement in support of Kenya's economic reform programme will hinge upon fundamental measures to address governance issues raised earlier in the context of the first year ESAF review."

The IMF, following guidelines approved last month to deal with official corruption, halted lending to Kenya one week ago and complained that the government had not done enough to crack down on widespread graft.

The IMF decision sent Kenyan financial markets into a tailspin and the shilling plunged to a new official low of 70.26 to the dollar on Thursday. Many foreign investors have been pulling their money out.
Finance Minister Musalia Mudavadi said in Nairobi on Thursday that Kenya was considering talks with the IMF on securing a second year of the loan arrangement, which he said was "still available."
He said the government was committed to sound fiscal and monetary policies.
